title: autotune: automate batching & caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Samantha Chen
release_notes: Automated default tuning for batching and prefix caching; new quantization profile registry and UEcon CLI + API for unit-econ reporting; no user-facing breaking changes.
description: Context: Customers and internal benchmarks show that suboptimal default batching/caching and generic quant profiles increase unit costs by 10-30% for common request shapes. This PR implements an end-to-end autotune flow to set safe defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, introduces a lightweight quantization profile registry for serving-time selection, and ships unit-economics tooling (UEcon) to compute per-token cost and recommended knobs. Changes include runtime heuristics, a CLI and API for offline analysis, and integration into the rollout pipeline. Highlights: 1) Autotune controller (runtime/autotune/optimizer.py) that observes request size distribution, latency SLO attainment, and throughput to set batching/window sizes and cache TTLs per model/route. 2) New defaults.yaml schema (runtime/batching/defaults.yaml) + migration code so existing deployments inherit safe defaults. 3) Quant profile registry (redwood-model-registry/quant_profiles) featuring curated profiles (q4_0, q5_e4, dynamic-mixed) and selection rules based on seqlen and hardware. 4) UEcon tooling (tools/uecon/compute_unit_econ.py and tools/uecon/cli.py) to estimate cost-per-request and generate recommended configuration changes; includes a lightweight API endpoint for Console integration. 5) Observability hooks and dashboards (console/dashboards/uecon.json, metrics/uecon_metrics) and alerting rules for cost regressions. 6) Tests: unit + integration tests and a small cost-sim harness used in CI to validate improvements. Checklist: - [x] Runtime heuristics implemented and covered by unit tests. - [x] Migration path for existing defaults added. - [x] Quantization profiles curated and validated against latency/cost tradeoffs. - [x] UEcon CLI + API implemented and documented. - [x] Console dashboards and alerts wired. - [x] End-to-end CI cost-sim passing. Testing & validation: ran the cost-sim benchmarks across p3/p4/gpu families and small/medium/large seqlen tiers; median unit cost reduction 18% with <2% P99 latency regression on heavy tails. Rollout plan: feature gated behind "autotune_defaults_v1" feature flag; staged rollout via canary groups with monitoring for latency SLO regressions and cost delta. If regressions exceed thresholds, controller will roll back to previous defaults automatically. Backwards compatibility: migration code ensures existing customer config is preserved and only augments missing defaults. Security & compliance: no secrets changes; KMS/HSM integrations unaffected. Notes for reviewers: focus review on optimizer heuristics and safety bounds in optimizer.py and the migration semantics in defaults.yaml; quantify any SLO risk. Related: ENG-2142 (autotune design), ENG-2198 (cost-sim harness), SUP-881 (customer report of cost spikes).
